title: Pañcadaśī — Chapter 1: Tattva-viveka
subtitle: Discrimination of Reality

source.edition: Vidyāraṇya, Panca-Dasi; A.K. Aruna, version 1.0 (2020), Chapter 1, verses 1.1–1.65

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 1
units.deva:
नमः श्री-शङ्करानन्द-गुरु-पादाम्बु-जन्मने।
सविलास-महा-मोह-ग्राह-ग्रासैक-कर्मणे॥
units.translation: Salutation to the lotus-like feet of my guru, Śrī Śaṅkarānanda, whose only job is to swallow the crocodile that is this grand delusion along with its effects.

gloss.en: to the lotus feet of Guru Śaṅkarānanda
whose sole work is to swallow great delusion with its play

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 2
units.deva:
तत्-पादाम्बु-रुह-द्वन्द्व-सेवा-निर्मल-चेतसाम्।
सुख-बोधाय तत्त्वस्य विवेदोऽयं विधीयते॥
units.translation: This discussion regarding reality and truth is presented for the easy understanding of those whose minds are least defiled via attendance at the two lotus-like feet of their.

gloss.en: for those whose minds are purified by service to those two lotus feet

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 3
units.deva:
शब्द-स्पर्शादयो वेद्या वैचित्र्याज् जागरे पृथक्।
ततो विभक्ता तत्-संविद् ऐक-रूप्यान् न भिद्यते॥
units.translation: The knowable beginning with sound, touch, etc. are separate in waking state due to their distinguishing characteristics, whereas the knower of these which is distinct from all of them does not differ because of its singular nature.

gloss.en: because it is one in nature

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 4
units.deva:
तथा स्वप्नेऽत्र वेद्यं तु न स्थिरं जागरे स्थिरम्।
तद्-भेदोऽतस् तयोः संविद् एकरूपा न भिद्यते॥
units.translation: Similarly in the dream state. Whereas a known object was stable in waking, here it is unstable. Thus there is a difference between them. the knower having the same nature does not differ.

gloss.en: here the known is not stable
one in nature, does not differ

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 5
units.deva:
सुप्तोत्थितस्य सौषुप्त-तमो-बोधो भवेत् स्मृतिः।
सा चावबुद्ध-विषयाऽवबुद्धं तत् तदा तमः॥
units.translation: For the one waking from deep sleep, there is remembrance that there was cognition of ignorance in deep sleep. A has as its object a cognition. At that time, that cognition is tamas.

gloss.en: awareness of the darkness of deep sleep
has what was known as its object
what was known then was ignorance

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 6
units.deva:
स बोधो विषयाद् भिन्नो न बोधात् स्वप्न-बोधवत्।
एवं स्थान-त्रयेऽप्येका संवित् तत्वद् दिनान्तरे॥
units.translation: That cognition is distinct from its object, but, like in dream, does not differ from itself. Thus the knower remains one only in the three states in that same way throughout the day.

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 7
units.deva:
मासाब्द-युग-कल्पेषु गतागम्येष्वनेकधा।
नोदेति नास्तम् एत्येका संविद् एषा स्वयं-प्रभा॥
units.translation: Throughout the countless months, years, ages and world cycles, both past and future, it neither rises nor sets. This one consciousness is self shining.

gloss.en: through months, years, ages, and cosmic cycles
through past and future in many ways

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 8
units.deva:
इयम् आत्मा परानन्दः पर-प्रेमास्पदं यतः।
मा न भूवं हि भूयासम् इति प्रेमात्मनीक्ष्यते॥
units.translation: This is oneself. It is ultimate fullness, because it is the natural abode of our greatest love. Love is seen in the self as, “May I indeed never cease to be,” “May I always be.”

gloss.en: may I never cease to be
thus love is seen directed toward oneself

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 9
units.deva:
तत् प्रेमात्मार्थम् अन्यत्र नैवम् अन्यार्थम् आत्मनि।
अतस् तत् परमं तेन परमानन्दतात्मनः॥
units.translation: Only for the sake of oneself is that love directed towards another, thus love towards oneself is never for the sake of another. Therefore, that is the highest. Hence the nature of the ultimate fullness belongs only to the self.

gloss.en: is for the sake of the Self
the Self is supreme bliss by nature

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 10
units.deva:
इत्थं सच्-चित्-परानन्द आत्मा युक्त्या तथाविधम्।
परं ब्रह्म तयोश् चैक्यं श्रुत्यन्तेषूपदिश्यते॥
units.translation: In this way, by this logic, existence-consciousness-fullness is the nature of oneself. Similarly is the ultimate brahman taught in the śrutis as the complete identity of these two.

gloss.en: the Self is existence, consciousness, and supreme bliss
the supreme Brahman is of the same nature

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 11
units.deva:
अभाने न परं प्रेम भाने न विषये स्पृहा।
अतो भानेऽप्यभाताऽसौ परमानन्दतात्मनः॥
units.translation: If the ultimate fullness nature of the self was not evident, there would be no ultimate love. if it was evident, there would be no attachment towards the objects of experience. Therefore, even though evident, it is not evident.

gloss.en: there is no longing for objects
the Self’s nature as supreme bliss

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 12
units.deva:
अध्येतृ-वर्ग-मध्यस्थ-पुत्राध्ययन-शब्दवत्।
भानेऽप्यभानं भानस्य प्रतिबन्धेन युज्यते॥
units.translation: Like the chanting voice of one’s child amongst a group of students, even though is evident, in regard to being evident, it is proper to take it as not evident, because of obstruction.

gloss.en: like the sound of one’s child reciting

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 13
units.deva:
प्रतिबन्धोऽस्ति-भातीति-व्यवहारार्ह-वस्तुनि।
तन्-निरस्य विरुद्धस्य तस्योत्पादनम् उच्यते॥
units.translation: Toward any object is applicable the experience, “It is” and it is evident”, there is an obstruction said to be the rejecting of this and imposing its opposite.

gloss.en: for an object fit for ordinary experience

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 14
units.deva:
तस्य हेतुः समानाभिहारः पुत्र-ध्वनि-श्रुतौ।
इहानादिर् अविद्यैव व्यामोहैक-निबन्धनम्॥
units.translation: The reason for that in regard to hearing the voice of one’s child is the mingling together as the same. Here, is beginningless ignorance. That alone is the obstruction leading to confusion.

gloss.en: confusion through mingling with similar sounds
is the sole basis of delusion

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 15
units.deva:
चिद्-आनन्दमय-ब्रह्म-प्रतिबिम्ब-समन्विता।
तमो-रजस्-सत्व-गुणा प्रकृतिर् द्विविधा च सा॥
units.translation: Prakṛti consists of the three guṇas: tamas, rajas, and sattva. It is imbued with a reflection of brahman consisting of consciousness-fullness. This prakṛti has two forms.

gloss.en: joined with a reflection of Brahman, whose nature is consciousness and bliss
having the qualities of tamas, rajas, and sattva

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 16
units.deva:
सत्व-शुद्ध्यविशुद्धिभ्यां मायाऽविद्ये च ते मते।
माया-बिम्बो वशी-कृत्य तां स्यात् सर्वज्ञ ईश्वरः॥
units.translation: From the perspective of its pure sattva alone, it is called ‘māyā’. From the perspective of its impurity, it is called ‘a-vidyā’. ‘Īśvara’ is the presence in that māyā, controlling that, and is all-knowing.

gloss.en: by purity and impurity of sattva

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 17
units.deva:
अविद्या-वशगस् त्वन्यस् तद्-वैचित्र्याद् अनेकधा।
सा कारण-शरीरं स्यात् प्राज्ञस् तत्राभिमानवान्॥
units.translation: But the other is under the spell of a-vidyā, and, because of the variety in that is taken as many. This is the causal body, and is the one who is identified in that. That is, it is called the ‘prājña’.*

gloss.en: the other is subject to ignorance
the one identified with it is prājña

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 18
units.deva:
तमः-प्रधान-प्रकृतेस् तद्-भोगायेश्वराज्ञया।
वियत्-पवन-तेजो-ऽम्बु-भुवो भूतानि जज्ञिरे॥
units.translation: Per the order wielded by the Lord, for the experiences of that, from tamas predominance of the aspects of prakṛti were born the elements: space, wind, fire, water, and earth.

gloss.en: from prakṛti in which tamas predominates
space, air, fire, water, and earth

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 19
units.deva:
सत्वांशैः पञ्चभिस् तेषां क्रमाद् धीन्द्रिय-पञ्चकम्।
श्रोत्र-त्वग्-अक्षि-रसन-घ्राणाख्यम् उपजायते॥
units.translation: From the sattva aspect of each of these five are indeed born separately the five sensory organs called: hearing, touching, seeing, tasting, and smelling.

gloss.en: from the five sattva portions of those elements
called hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 20
units.deva:
तैर् अन्तः-करणं सर्वैर् वृत्ति-भेदेन तद् द्विधा।
मनो विमर्श-रूपं स्याद् बुद्धिः स्यान् निश्चयात्मिका॥
units.translation: From all these is the antaḥ-karaṇa with different forms and functions. That is of two types. One type is called the manas where the thoughts have the nature of vimarśa. The other type is buddhi where the thoughts have the nature of niścaya.

gloss.en: manas has the nature of deliberation

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 21
units.deva:
रजोंशैः पञ्चभिस् तेषां क्रमात् कर्मेन्द्रयाणि तु।
वाक्-पाणि-पाद-पायुपस्थाभिधानानि जज्ञिरे॥
units.translation: From the rajas aspect of the five separately are born the five organs of action called: voicing, handling, moving, excreting, and procreating.

gloss.en: from the five rajas portions of those elements
called speech, hands, feet, excretion, and generation

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 22
units.deva:
तैः सर्वैः सहितैः प्राणो वृत्ति-भेदात् स पञ्चधा।
प्राणोऽपानः समानश्चोदान-व्यानौ च ते पुनः॥
units.translation: From all these as a whole comes the prāṇa, which is of five types due to different forms and functions called: outward energy, downward energy, assimilating energy, upward energy, and circulating energy.

gloss.en: prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna, and vyāna

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 23
units.deva:
बुद्धि-कर्मेन्द्रिय-प्राण-पञ्चकैर् मनसा धिया।
शरीरं सप्त-दशभिः सूक्ष्मं तल्-लिङ्गम् उच्यते॥
units.translation: The manas, buddhi, along with the five each organs of sensing and of action, plus the five prāṇas – as seventeen make up the subtle body, also called the liṅga-śarīra.

gloss.en: with intellect, organs of action, and the five vital airs
that is called the liṅga body

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 24
units.deva:
प्राज्ञस् तत्राभिमानेन तैजसत्वं प्रपद्यते।
हिरण्य-गर्भताम् ईशस् तयोर् व्यष्टि-समष्टिता॥
units.translation: Through identification there this prājña attains taijasatva at its individual level and the nature of the Lord in the form of Hiraṇya-garbha at its cosmic level.

gloss.en: the Lord attains the state of Hiraṇyagarbha

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 25
units.deva:
समष्टिर् ईशः सर्वेषां स्वात्म-तादात्म्य-वेदनात्।
तद्-अभावात् ततोऽन्ये तु कथ्यन्ते व्यष्टि-संज्ञया॥
units.translation: The Lord is the totality of all this due to the sense of identification in all of their natures, sva-ātman, their subtle bodies,. The one who is other than that one, though, in the absence of that they call the individual knower.

gloss.en: the Lord is the totality of all
through recognition of identity with their own Self

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 26
units.deva:
तद्-भोगाय पुनर्-भोग्य-भोगायतन-जन्मने।
पञ्ची-करोति भगवान् प्रयेकं वियद्-आदिकम्॥
units.translation: To provide objects of experiences for those, and provide for births into more fit receptacles of these experiences, the Lord mixed each one, beginning with space, five-fold*.

gloss.en: to produce objects, enjoyment, and places of experience

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 27
units.deva:
द्विधा विधाय चैकैकं चतुर्धा प्रथमं पुनः।
स्वस्वेतर-द्वितीयांशैर् योजनात् पञ्च पञ्च ते॥
units.translation: proportioning into two portions and then the first portion into four portions*, so that the second portion is itself alone and each of the other four portions are the other. From this combination there are five each consisting of five.

gloss.en: then dividing the first part into four
with the secondary portions of the other elements
thus each of the five is fivefold

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 28
units.deva:
तैर् अण्डस् तत्र भुवनं भोग्य-भोगाश्रयोद्भवः।
हिरण्य-गर्भः स्थूलेऽस्मिन् देहे वैश्वा-नरो भवेत्॥
units.translation: As these was the source. In that, the universe arose, which then became the abode for the experiences. Hiraṇya-garbha is then present in this gross.* In the body it would be called the vaiśvā-nara.

gloss.en: arising as the support for objects and experience

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 29
units.deva:
तैजसा विश्वतां याता देव-तिर्यङ्-नरादयः।
ते पराग्-दर्शिनः प्रत्यक्-तत्त्व-बोध-विवर्जिताः॥
units.translation: comes to be the taijasas and they become known as the viśva as a deity, animal, human, etc.. All of these experience only the external and are without true knowledge of the within.

gloss.en: devoid of knowledge of the inner reality

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 30
units.deva:
कुर्वते कर्म भोगाय कर्म कर्तुं च भुञ्जते।
नद्यां कीटा इवावर्ताद् आवर्तान्तरम् आशु ते।
व्रजन्तो जन्मनो जन्म लभन्ते नैव निर्वृतिम्॥
units.translation: These do action to enjoy and enjoy to do action. Like worms swiftly moving in a river from one whirlpool to another, these individuals move from birth to birth, never gaining peace.

gloss.en: they act for the sake of experience
and experience in order to act
they pass from birth to birth

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 31
units.deva:
सत्-कर्म-परिपाकात् ते करुणा-निधिनोद्धृताः।
प्राप्य तीर-तरु-च्छायां विश्राम्यन्ति यथा-सुखम्॥
units.translation: Due to the maturation of their good karma, a few are rescued by someone who is a reservoir of compassion. Gaining this shade of a tree on the bank, they rest in that pleasure.

gloss.en: through the ripening of good action
are lifted up by the ocean of compassion
having reached the shade of a tree on the bank

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 32
units.deva:
उपदेशम् अवाप्यैवम् आचार्यात् तत्त्व-दर्शिनः।
पञ्च-कोश-विवेकेन लभन्ते निर्वृतिं पराम्॥
units.translation: Similarly, gain this teaching from a teacher who knows this truth. Through the discernment of pañca-kośa, they attain ultimate peace.

gloss.en: from a teacher who sees truth
through discernment of the five sheaths

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 33
units.deva:
अन्नं प्राणो मनो बुद्धिर् आननश्चेति पञ्च ते।
कोशास् तैर् आवृतः स्वात्मा विस्मृत्या संसृतिं व्रजेत्॥
units.translation: These five kośas are: this food, energy, mind, knowledge, and pleasure. Trapped by these as though they were one’s very self, and oblivious they undergo saṃsāra.

gloss.en: food, vital energy, mind, intellect, and bliss
the Self is covered by them

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 34
units.deva:
स्यात् पञ्ची-कृत-भूतोत्थो देहः स्थूलोऽन्न-संज्ञकः।
लिङ्गे तु राजसैः प्राणैः प्राणः कर्मेन्द्रियैः सह॥
units.translation: The gross body born of the five-folded gross elements is known as the anna. Whereas, within the liṅga body is the prāṇa consisting of the rajas in the form of the prāṇas, along with the karmendriyas.

gloss.en: with vital forces born of rajas
vital function together with the organs of action

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 35
units.deva:
सात्विकैर् धीन्द्रियैः साकं विमर्शात्मा मनोमयः।
तैर् एव साकं विज्ञानमयो धीर् निश्चयात्मिका॥
units.translation: The mind having the nature of examining of the sātvika, along with the organs of perceptual knowledge, is known as the mental. The intellect having the nature of resolve, also along with those, is known as the intellectual.

gloss.en: together with the knowledge organs born of sattva

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 36
units.deva:
कारणे सत्त्वम् आनन्दमयो मोदादि-वृत्तिभिः।
तत्-तत्-कोशैस् तु तादात्म्याद् आत्मा तत्-तन्-मयो भवेत्॥
units.translation: The sattva in the causal body is with modification of moda, etc., and is known as ānanda-maya. Due to identification with each one of the kośas then the self would be assumed to have the natures of each one of them.

gloss.en: with joy and its other forms
the Self seems to take on its nature

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 37
units.deva:
अन्वय-व्यतिरेकाभ्यां पञ्च-कोश-विवेकतः।
स्वात्मानं तत उद्धृत्य परं ब्रह्म प्रपद्यते॥
units.translation: By discerning of each of the five kośas through anvaya-vyatireka, then one draws out just one’s self and arrives at limitless brahman.

gloss.en: through discernment of the five sheaths
separating one’s own Self from them

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 38
units.deva:
अभाने स्थूल-देहस्य स्वप्ने यद्-भानम् आत्मनः।
सोऽन्वयो व्यतिरेकस् तद् भानेऽन्यानवभासनम्॥
units.translation: In dream, wherein there is the non-appearance of this physical body, the continued presence of ātman is the anvaya. the non-appearance of the physical body while that is manifestly present is its vyatireka.

gloss.en: when the gross body is absent
the Self is present in dream

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 39
units.deva:
लिङ्गाभाने सुषुप्तौ स्याद् आत्मनो भानम् अन्वयः।
व्यतिरेकस् तु तद्-भाने लिङ्गस्याभानम् उच्यते॥
units.translation: in deep sleep, wherein there is the non-appearance of the subtle body, the continued presence of ātman is the anvaya. Whereas, the non-appearance of the subtle body while that is manifestly present is said to be its vyatireka.

gloss.en: when the subtle body is absent in deep sleep
is said to be the absence of the subtle body

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 40
units.deva:
तद्-विवेक-विविक्ताः स्युः कोशाः प्राण-मनो-धियः।
ते हि तत्र गुणावस्था-भेद-मात्रात् पृथक् कृताः॥
units.translation: Those kośas consisting of prāṇa, manas, and intellect are distinguished by this discernment from that. In that case, they are also distinguished simply by the difference in their natures and their location.

gloss.en: of vital energy, mind, and intellect
only by differences of quality and state

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 41
units.deva:
सुषुप्त्यभाने भानं तु समाधावात्मानोऽन्वयः।
व्यतिरेकस् त्वात्म-भाने सुषुप्त्यनवभासनम्॥
units.translation: Whereas, in samādhi* which is also without suṣupti, there is the anvaya,. And the non-appearance of deep sleep while the self is manifestly present is its vyatireka.

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 42
units.deva:
यथा मुञ्जाद् इषीकैवम् आत्मा युक्त्या समुद्धृतः।
शरीर-त्रितयाद् धीरैः परं ब्रह्मैव जायते॥
units.translation: Like the internal pith from the muñja grass, so the ātman is carefully separated by the wise with logic from the three bodies. Then one is reborn as the ultimate brahman alone.

gloss.en: as the pith is drawn from muñja grass

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 43
units.deva:
परापरात्मनोर् एवं युक्त्या संभावितैकता।
तत् त्वम् अस्यादि-वाक्यैस् सा भाग-त्यागेन लक्ष्यते॥
units.translation: In this way is manifestly taught with logic one’s identity with the para-ātman from the a-para-ātman. this is indicated by eliminating aspects through the vākyas, such as ‘tat tvam asi’, etc.

gloss.en: of the higher and lower Self
by statements such as ‘That thou art’
by giving up the incompatible parts

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 44
units.deva:
जगतो यद् उपादानं मायाम् आदाय तामसीम्।
निमित्तं शुद्ध-सत्त्वां ताम् उच्यते ब्रह्म तद्-गिरा॥
units.translation: By the word ‘tad’ is referenced brahman which has taken on māyā through her tamas aspect which would be the material cause of the universe and through her pure sattva aspect which would be the intelligent cause.

gloss.en: that which is the material cause
that is called Brahman by the word ‘That’

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 45
units.deva:
यदा मलिन-सत्त्वां तां काम-कर्मादि-दूषिताम्।
आदत्ते तत् परं ब्रह्म त्वं-पदेन तदोच्यते॥
units.translation: By the word ‘tvam’ is referenced that same ultimate brahman, whenever it has taken on sattva mixed up and defiled with desires and activities, etc.

gloss.en: tainted by desire, action, and the like

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 46
units.deva:
त्रितयीम् अपि तां मुक्त्वा परस्-पर-विरोधिनीम्।
अखण्डं सच्-चिद्-आनन्दं महा-वाक्येन लक्ष्यते॥
units.translation: But eliminating these three features that are incompatible with each other, no distinction is indicated by this mahā-vākya, which is their existence-consciousness-fullness *.

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 47
units.deva:
सोऽयम्-इत्यादि-वाक्येषु विरोधात् तद्-इदन्तयोः।
त्यागेन भागयोर् एक आश्रयो लक्ष्यते यथा॥
units.translation: The same as in declarations such as, ‘That is this ’, by eliminating the two features, in the form of ‘that’ and ‘this’, then the one basis is indicated.

gloss.en: in statements such as ‘That is this’

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 48
units.deva:
मायाऽविद्ये विहायैवम् उपाधी पर-जीवयोः।
अखण्डं सच्-चिद्-आनन्दं पर ब्रह्मैव लक्ष्यते॥
units.translation: Eliminating both māyā and a-vidya upādhis of the Lord and the jīva, their non-distinction is indicated as brahman only, which is their existence-consciousness-fullness.

gloss.en: of the Lord and the individual

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 49
units.deva:
स-विकल्पस्य लक्ष्यत्वे लक्ष्यस्य स्याद् अवस्तुता।
निर्-विकल्पस्य लक्ष्यत्वं न दृष्टं न च सम्भवि॥
units.translation: If the nature of what is being indicated is sa-vikalpa, then the indicated lacks reality. But if the nature of what is being indicated is nir-vikalpa, then is neither seen nor possible.

gloss.en: if it is the object indicated

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 50
units.deva:
विकल्पो निर्-विकल्पस्य स-विकल्पस्य वा भवेत्।
आद्ये व्याहतिर् अन्यत्रानवस्थाऽत्माश्रयादयः॥
units.translation: If having no features can be figured out, then this starts out as contradiction. If having features can be figured out, then there will be anyatra-an-avasthā or ātma-āśraya, etc.

gloss.en: of what is distinctionless or qualified
infinite regress, self-dependence, and the like

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 51
units.deva:
इदं गुण-क्रिया-जाति-द्रव्य-सम्बन्ध-वस्तुषु।
समं तेन स्व-रूपस्य सर्वम् एतद् इतीष्यताम्॥
units.translation: This same towards any object having a quality, having an action, having a category, having a substance, and having a relationship. Hence, it is instead to be understood that all this is upon my very nature.

gloss.en: for things with qualities, actions, kinds, substances, and relations

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 52
units.deva:
विकल्प-तद्-अभावाभ्याम् असंस्पृष्टात्म-वस्तुनि।
विकल्पितत्व-लक्ष्यत्व-सम्बन्धाद्यास् तु कल्पिताः॥
units.translation: When the reality of the self is untouched by either attributes or the lack of them, then the nature of being attributed, of being logically indicated, of having any relationships, etc. are all assumptions.

gloss.en: in the Self, untouched by either
attribution, indication, relation, and the rest

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 53
units.deva:
इत्थं वाक्यैस् तद्-अर्थानुसन्धानं श्रवणं भवेत्।
युक्त्या सम्भावितत्वानुसन्धानं मननं तु तत्॥
units.translation: Thus, what is called śravaṇa involves scrutiny as to its meaning intended by these statements. Whereas, manana should involve scrutiny as to its validity by means of logic.

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 54
units.deva:
ताभ्यां निर्विचिकित्सेऽर्थे चेतसः स्थापितस्य यत्।
एकतानत्वम् एतद्धि निदिध्यासनम् उच्यते॥
units.translation: What indeed is called nididhyāsana is the abidance of a steadied mind upon the doubtless meaning arrived at by these two.

gloss.en: on the meaning free from doubt
of the mind that has been settled

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 55
units.deva:
ध्यातृ-ध्याने परित्यज्य क्रमाद् ध्येयैक-गोचरम्।
निवात-दीपवच् चित्तं समाधिर् अभिधीयते॥
units.translation: In stages, eliminating as an agent and the action of meditating, where the mind, like a flame protected from the wind, has as its scope only the one dhyeya, is called samādhi.

gloss.en: with only the object of meditation as its field
like a lamp in a windless place

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 56
units.deva:
वृत्तयस् तु तदानीम् अज्ञाता अप्यात्म-गोचराः।
स्मरणाद् अनुमीयन्ते व्युत्थितस्य समुत्थितात्॥
units.translation: Although, at that time this flow of thoughts, whose scope is only the self, are not known, and they, after one has arisen from being thus immersed, are inferred to be there from a memory.

gloss.en: having the Self as their object

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 57
units.deva:
वृत्तीनाम् अनुवृत्तिस् तु प्रयत्नात् प्रथमाद् अपि।
अदृष्टासकृद्-अभ्यास-संस्कार-सचिवाद् भवेत्॥
units.translation: The continuous flow is by previous effort and by the assistance of latent tendencies created by repeated practice and as one’s unseen.

gloss.en: assisted by unseen impressions of repeated practice

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 58
units.deva:
यथा-दीपो-निवातस्थ इत्यादिभिर् अनेकधा।
भगवान् इमम् एवार्थम् अर्जुनाय न्यरूपयत्॥
units.translation: This very same idea, Lord pointed out to Arjuna in various ways by such statements, ‘Like the oil lamp in a windless place’.

gloss.en: by examples such as a lamp in a windless place

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 59
units.deva:
अनादाविह संसारे सञ्चिताः कर्म-कोटयः।
अनेन विलयं यान्ति शुद्धो धर्मो विवर्धते॥
units.translation: Here in beginningless saṃsāra are accumulated countless karmas. By this those are kept in remission, and there arises pure dharma.

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 60
units.deva:
धर्म-मेघम् इमं प्राहुस् समाधिं योग-वित्तमाः।
वर्षत्येष यतो धर्मामृत-धारास् सहस्रशः॥
units.translation: Experts in yoga call this samādhi a rain-cloud of dharma, because it pours countless showers of immortal dharma.

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 61
units.deva:
अमुना वासना-जले निःशेषं प्रविलापिते।
स-मूलोन्मूलिते पुण्य-पापाख्ये कर्म-सञ्चये॥
units.translation: By that, one brings about the complete abatement, by its very root, of one’s accumulated karma, called puṇya-pāpa, which as a pool of vāsanās.

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 62
units.deva:
वाक्यम् अप्रतिबद्धम् सत् प्राक् परोक्षावभासिते।
करामलकवद् बोधम् अपरोक्षं प्रसूयते॥
units.translation: The true words of the teaching, freed from obstacles, which previously were viewed as parokṣa, now bears fruit as direct knowledge, like āmalaka fruit in the hand.

gloss.en: like a fruit in the palm

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 63
units.deva:
परोक्षं ब्रह्म-विज्ञानं शाब्दं देशिक-पूर्वकम्।
बुद्धि-पूर्व-कृतं पापं कृत्स्नं दहति वह्निवत्॥
units.translation: The assimilated knowledge of brahman, which was indirect and which was introduced by a teacher through words – now, like a fire, completely burns up the pāpa committed prior to this knowledge.

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 64
units.deva:
अपरोक्षात्म-विज्ञानं शाब्दं देशिक-पूर्वकम्।
संसार-कारणाज्ञान-तमसश् चण्ड-भास्करः॥
units.translation: The assimilated knowledge, having the nature of not being out of reach of one’s experience, which was introduced by a teacher through their words, like the bright light of the sun, out of the darkness of ignorance that is the material cause of saṃsāra.

gloss.en: the darkness of ignorance, cause of saṃsāra

units.label: Chapter 1 · Verse 65
units.deva:
इत्थं तत्त्व-विवेकं विधाय विधिवन्-मनस् समाधाय।
विगलित-संसृति-बन्धः प्राप्नोति परं पदं नरो न चिरात्॥
units.translation: Thus, one starts distinguishing through tattva-viveka and begins to settle the instructed mind. Before long, the retained notions of bondage come to an end and the person attains the ultimate abode.

gloss.en: freed from the bond of transmigration
